videos.review: Corvo goes into a clear Blink aim (wide stance, left arm reaching forward, sword low). The native blue departure burst plays at the origin and the arrival burst and smoke at the target, where he lands in a natural standing recovery. He is then moved back to the origin for the second cast, which is aimed and cancelled; that reset shows a brief dark streak but is a fixture move, not part of the power.

Same sequence: aim pose, departure FX at the origin, arrival with smoke at the target, standing recovery, fixture reset, a second aim that is cancelled, then a planted idle. Limbs stay intact, with no T-pose or stuck pose.

summary: Blink aim, native departure/arrival world FX, discrete arrival and the cancelled second aim all read correctly on the partner. Only a dark streak during the lab's reset back to the origin is visible, and it is not part of the power.

videos.review: Dark scene, so the clip was cropped and brightened. Standing armed Corvo raises his left arm forward into the Possession aim, holds it for about 1 s with the sword arm swinging back, then lowers smoothly into the armed idle with his feet planted. The take only covers entry and aim on an empty target: no possession of a target, loop or exit is shown.

summary: The empty-target Possession entry and aim, and the recovery to idle, read naturally. The possessed loop and the exit with a real target are not recorded, so that is a coverage gap rather than a visual defect.

videos.review: Standing armed Corvo makes two clear casts: he leans, sweeps the left arm out and up with the sword held low, then returns to the armed idle. Timing is plausible, feet stay planted and limbs stay intact. No remote time-stop world effect is visible, which matches the scope.

From a high angle and dark (cropped and brightened), crouched Corvo moves, casts with the left hand forward, then twice rises into a hunched, wide-armed release pose before settling back into the crouch. It is recognizable and continuous. The crouched release reads less cleanly than the standing one (it is a generic-looking spread-arm pose), which is polish. The static crouch-guard v50 take was also checked: a short crouched cast and a clean return.

summary: Standing and crouched Bend Time casts and releases are recognizable and recover cleanly. The crouched release pose is a little generic, and no world time effect is shown (out of scope).

videos.review: Crouched armed Corvo thrusts his left palm forward while pulling the sword arm back and stays crouched. The native wind-streak world effect appears in front of him for the cast, and he returns to the crouched idle. Two casts, both clean.

Holstered standing Corvo turns, steps into a wide stance and thrusts his left arm with the right arm swept back. The native wind streaks appear, then he steps back to the upright holstered idle. Two casts with good weight shift and feet planted.

summary: Windblast reads correctly in the crouched-armed and standing-holstered contexts, and the native wind streak world effect is visible on the observer.

videos.review: Dark scene, so it was brightened. Standing armed Corvo winds up into a wide summoning stance (left hand extended, sword raised behind), holds it for about 2 s, then recovers to the armed idle. The body reads well, but no rats are visible on the observer's floor in this take (its scope says peer playback creates no rats).

Crouched Corvo walks forward, then casts from the crouch with his left arm extended low, holds, and at the end stands up over about 0.3 s into the armed idle. The stand-up is a little quick but blended rather than popped. No rats are visible.

summary: The Swarm cast body reads well standing and crouched-moving. No native rats are visible on the observer in the reviewed takes, so the world presentation is not shown on video.

videos.review: Emily holds a clear Far Reach aim (left arm extended, sword raised). The native dark tether extends from her left hand to the target, she is pulled across fast, lands with the native purple impact ring and recovers to standing. She is then reset to the origin, where a second aim is cancelled back to idle.
Same flow: aim, pull with impact FX at the target, standing recovery, a reset streak back to the origin (fixture), a second aim, and a planted idle. No limb breakage or stuck pose.

summary: The Far Reach aim, native tether, pull, impact and recovery read correctly. The only visible artifact is the reset streak back to the origin, which is a fixture move.

videos.review: At the gallery railing, Emily turns, points her left arm at the target across the hall and holds it for about 1.2 s (the Domino link gesture), then returns to idle. The glowing native mark is visible on the target and fades later. Framing is poor: she sits at the right screen edge, partly behind the observer's first-person blade, and the observer camera drifts.

Dark corridor, so it was brightened. Standing armed Emily raises and points her left arm (Domino gesture) with the sword held out, then settles into the armed idle. The gesture is clear and the recovery smooth.

The camera frames the marked guard: the native gold Domino mark sparks and glow appear over his head. Emily's body is not in frame, so it can't be judged here; this take is only evidence of the world effect.

summary: The Domino point-and-link gesture and its recovery read correctly, and the native mark effect appears on the target. Framing in v218 is cramped at the screen edge.

videos.review: Emily turns and raises her left arm up and forward into the Mesmerize aim, holds it for about 2 s, then releases and recovers to the armed idle with her feet planted. The observer camera then cuts to the target, where the native Void-spirit column appears and is removed on interruption.
Same cast gesture and recovery. The native spirit model appears at the target area and later expires cleanly.

summary: The Mesmerize cast body reads naturally, and the native spirit world effect appears and clears on the observer.

videos.review: Emily holsters her sword and drops smoothly into the low Shadow Walk crawl. She crawls forward and back with her limbs moving and grounded, then rises, redraws the sword and settles into a sneaking stance. Her body keeps its normal material (the shadow material is not applied), and no attack is shown.
Same entry, crawl and exit. Faint dark ash particles are visible near her hands during the crawl. The standing idle at the start holds her arms slightly out (a bit stiff, but not a bind pose).

summary: Shadow Walk entry, crawl and exit read correctly as functional coverage. The shadow material and attacks are not shown, and the native particles are subtle.

videos.review: Standing armed Corvo plays short out-of-mana flinches with the left hand and native hand smoke, the observer's pause menu interrupts, and after resume he recovers to the armed idle. Note: from about 13.5 s to the end he steps into a squarer, upright relaxed stance (arms hanging, sword pointing down, yaw rotated about 30 degrees) and holds it static; source-resume v51 ends the same way, receiver-stop v51 does not. It is blended, not popped, and likely the fixture restore, but it is worth a check.

Crouched armed Corvo half-rises with a left-hand flick for each failed cast, then drops back into the crouch. The native blue hand-smoke failure effect is visible on the left hand, and the crouch is retained.

summary: Corvo's Bend Time out-of-mana failures and pause recovery read correctly. A late relaxed-stance switch after the resume tests should be checked, and no Emily or other-power interruption recordings exist (outside the bound scope).
